subject: Data lifecycle decision log — PHI retention thresholds & scrub strategies for teletriage pilot
messages:
From: Dr. Aisha Qureshi <aisha.qureshi@harborcare.org>
To: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Teletriage pilot — retention/erasure questions

Hi Sean / Marissa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough today. Our privacy office asked for a pragmatic recommendation for the pilot data lifecycle: we need a retention policy for incoming teletriage transcripts that contain PHI and PII, plus a short list of redaction approaches you support. Specifically: 
- What is a reasonable default retention window for raw transcripts during pilot evaluation?
- Can Redwood support field-level redaction of phone numbers and SSNs at ingest?
- For post-hoc erasure requests, what does the record look like in logs (are de-identified samples retained)?

I'm attaching a sanitized sample schema and the dataset preview. We plan to onboard 2 clinics and want to finalize this by next Friday.

Best,
Aisha
Dr. Aisha Qureshi
Clinical Informatics Lead, HarborCare

Attachments: harborcare-teletriage-data-schema.csv (CSV stub), dataset-preview.json (omitted)
From: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Dr. Aisha Qureshi <aisha.qureshi@harborcare.org>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Teletriage pilot — retention/erasure questions

Hi Aisha — short answers up front, details below:

1) Pilot raw transcript retention: configurable, reasonable default 30 days for raw text during active eval; 180 days for de-identified analytic data.
2) Field-level redaction at ingest: yes, we support regex-based and schema-driven redaction (phone, SSN, MRNs) before any model processing.
3) Erasure requests: we can fully remove raw text and associated KV caches; we retain an audit stub (timestamp, request id, hash) for 90 days to support compliance investigations.

Detailed notes attached and a suggested worksheet for retention tiers. We'll loop in Compliance for the formal sign-off.

Next step: Marissa, can you propose a matrix with gating conditions (pilot success metrics) that would extend the raw retention window beyond 30 days?

Thanks,
Sean
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed-retention-matrix-v1.xlsx (stub)
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Dr. Aisha Qureshi <aisha.qureshi@harborcare.org>
Date: Tue, 31 Aug 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Teletriage pilot — retention/erasure questions

Thanks Aisha, Sean — sketched a simple decision matrix below to keep the pilot moving:

- Raw transcript (unredacted): default 30 days during pilot. Extension to 90 days allowed only if: (a) site-level IRB or legal waiver provided OR (b) aggregated quality review requires longer windows and patient consent documented.
- Token-level caches / KV cache: evict after 24 hours by default; can be warmed for 7 days for throughput-sensitive routes with explicit justification.
- De-identified analytics dataset (no direct identifiers): retain up to 180 days for model evaluation, must be stored on dedicated tenant if HarborCare requests isolation.
- Field redaction: ingest-time removal of phone/SSN/MRN is implemented via pipeline step; we recommend hashing identifiers where downstream mapping is required and storing mapping outside Redwood control plane if HarborCare wants full separation.

Action items:
1) HarborCare to confirm whether they will provide a signed data processing addendum specifying mapping storage preferences.
2) Compliance (Neha) to confirm audit stub retention period and language for SOC documentation.

Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2026 14:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Teletriage pilot — retention/erasure questions

Hi all — quick compliance confirmation and suggested wording for contractual language: 

- Audit stub: we keep a non-reversible hash + action metadata for 90 days. The hash cannot be used to reconstruct PHI; it is stored only for incident correlation.
- Erasure SLA: standard pilot erasure request processed within 7 business days; we will remove raw transcripts, cached keys, and any derivative model fine-tuning buckets. Analytics derivatives that are impossible to reverse (aggregates) will be documented and retained only if explicit consent is present.
- Redaction options: ingest-time redaction (recommended) must run prior to any third-party observability exports; alternately, customers can request in-region private deployment to keep raw data off our hosted control plane.

Proposed contract clause (short): 
"Redwood will implement ingest-time removal of direct identifiers on specified fields and process erasure requests to delete raw transcripts and associated caches within the agreed SLA. Redwood will retain an audit stub (non-reversible hash and meta) for 90 days for compliance purposes"

I'll review the retention matrix file and send minor edits.

-Neha
Legal & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Teletriage pilot — retention/erasure questions — final decisions

Aisha — wrapping up the thread with agreed pilot defaults and next steps. Please confirm this in reply so we can attach to the DPA.

Agreed pilot defaults (Redwood / HarborCare):
1) Raw transcripts: 30-day default retention window. Extension to 90 days only with documented patient consent or legal/IRB waiver.
2) KV/token caches: 24-hour eviction default. Option to extend to 7 days for specific routes with formal justification.
3) Ingest-time redaction: Redwood will run schema-driven redaction for phone numbers and SSNs before model inference. Hash-only mapping will be used if HarborCare requires reversible linkage; mapping must be stored in HarborCare-managed store.
4) Erasure requests: Redwood will delete raw text and evict KV caches within 7 business days; an audit stub (non-reversible hash + timestamp + request id) will be retained for 90 days.
5) Analytics: de-identified aggregates only, retained up to 180 days; any derivative that could re-identify individuals requires consent and must be documented in the DPA.

Next steps:
- Aisha: confirm acceptance or flag items by EOD Friday; provide DPA contact.
- Redwood: update proposed-retention-matrix-v1.xlsx with compliance edits and return updated file.
- Compliance: Neha will draft the exact DPA clause text for inclusion.

Thanks and talk soon,
Sean
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
